newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu keeps out of public eye.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu keeps out of public eye.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, back home to salvage what remains of his authority in the face of rebel advances, kept out of the public eye on Saturday, further fuelling speculation about his health.

Mobutu, who left hospital in Europe on Wednesday after a fresh bout of cancer treatment, returned home from France on Friday on his private jet but has not been seen in public since climbing abroad the plane in Nice.
"The president will resume his normal duties today," state television reported on Saturday. His aides said on Friday night that the veteran leader had had a "difficult" journey home and was resting.
Mobutu, 66, has spent most of his time in Europe since having prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.
Banza Mukalay, number two in Mobutu's Popular Revolutionary Movement (MPR), told Reuters the president was likely to resume his full duties on Sunday.
"He is likely to resume tomorrow. He will receive the South African deputy president (Thabo Mbeki) in Kinshasa tomorrow," Banza said.
Some Zaire watchers expect Mobutu to begin in ernest on Monday, others say he will get down to work earlier.
"The president has to rest but a responsible government has to be formed first, that will correctly carry out its duties," Bemba Saolona, a Mobutu supporter, said.
"The president has so far received nobody. He is a bit angry. He will take important decisions. He cannot let things drift," Bemba, an influential member of parliament, added.
Mobutu sent away an official airport welcoming party, which included Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo and senior government members and military officers.
Mobutu aides said on Friday he was tired. Some officials said he was reluctant to be seen being helped down the aircraft steps.

Quoting a presidential aide, the leading independent newspaper Le Soft said Mobutu had in fact refused to shake hands with "traitors" -- officials who could not help the army win the war -- at the airport.
Opposition newspapers ask whether Mobutu's retun will have any effect on the advances by the rebels, who want to topple him and took up arms in October. The rebels now hold one fifth of Zaire.
Mobutu returned from France on Friday, after fresh successes by rebels who are fighting to topple him. He has spent most of his time in Europe since prostate cancer surgery there in August.

"I have returned not to devote myself to Mobutu's interests nor to Mobutu's fortune as you write from time to time but to the higher interests of Zaire," he told journalists. "That is to say our unity, our territorial integrity."
Asked how he felt, Mobutu, who left hospital in Monaco after fresh cancer treatment on Wednesday, replied: "I feel the way I look."
Mobutu, 66, has ruled Zaire since seizing power in an army coup in 1965.
